title: Histone Extraction HLB Protocol
author: Sigrid Verhelst
materials: Start from a dry (snap-frozen) cell pellet

steps.title: Prepare and add hypotonic lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Make hypotonic lysis buffer (HLB) containing 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0, 1 mM KCl, 1.5 mM MgCl₂, 1 mM DTT, 1 mM PMSF, Halt Protease and Phosphatase Inhibitor Cocktail 100× (catalog 78440) and phosphatase inhibitor cocktails II and III (P5726 and P0044, Sigma‑Aldrich; add 1 mL of each cocktail per 100 mL of buffer). Add 200 µL of this buffer to each pellet of 1 × 10⁶ cells and resuspend gently.

steps.title: Lyse cells by rotation
steps.instruction: Rotate the suspension for 30 min at 4 °C to promote cell‑membrane lysis by mechanical shear.

steps.title: Pellet nuclei by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at 10 000 g for 10 min at 4 °C and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Resuspend nuclei in 0.4 N HCl
steps.instruction: Resuspend the nuclear pellet in 0.4 N hydrochloric acid by soft pipetting until no clumps remain; add 125 µL of HCl per 1 × 10⁶ cells and vortex briefly if necessary.

steps.title: Acid incubation for histone solubilization
steps.instruction: Incubate the acid suspension on a rotator for 30 min at 4 °C to lyse nuclei and solubilize histones.

steps.title: Clarify lysate by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Spin the sample at 16 000 g for 10 min at 4 °C to pellet debris.

steps.title: Transfer acid supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully transfer the clear supernatant (which contains the histones) to a new Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Precipitate histones with TCA
steps.instruction: Add trichloroacetic acid (TCA) drop‑by‑drop to the supernatant until a final TCA concentration of 33 % is reached; invert the tube several times until the solution becomes milky.

steps.title: Incubate precipitation on ice
steps.instruction: Place the tube on ice for 30 min to allow histone precipitation.

steps.title: Pellet histones by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 16 000 g for 10 min at 4 °C to collect the histone pellet.

steps.title: Discard supernatant carefully
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant without disturbing the pellet (the pellet may be invisible).

steps.title: Wash pellet with ice‑cold acetone (first)
steps.instruction: Add enough ice‑cold acetone to fully cover the pellet (do not resuspend) to remove residual TCA.

steps.title: Centrifuge after first acetone wash
steps.instruction: Spin at 16 000 g for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Remove acetone supernatant
steps.instruction: Discard the acetone supernatant.

steps.title: Wash pellet with cold acetone (second)
steps.instruction: Add cold acetone again to fully cover the pellet (do not resuspend) for a second TCA removal.

steps.title: Centrifuge after second acetone wash
steps.instruction: Spin at 16 000 g for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Remove acetone supernatant
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Resuspend histones in MilliQ water
steps.instruction: Resuspend the dried pellet in 50 µL MilliQ water per 1 × 10⁶ cells.

steps.title: Optional SDS‑PAGE preparation
steps.instruction: Transfer material equivalent to 400 000 cells to a new Eppendorf tube for SDS‑PAGE. If clumps remain, centrifuge at 16 000 g for 10 min at 4 °C and transfer the clear supernatant to a fresh tube.

steps.title: Air‑dry acetone‑washed pellet at room temperature
steps.instruction: Leave the tube open at room temperature for 30 min until all acetone has evaporated.

steps.title: Vacuum‑dry samples and store
steps.instruction: Dry the samples in a SpeedVac, then store both Eppendorf tubes (for propionylation/digestion and for SDS‑PAGE) at –20 °C or –80 °C until further use.
